impact:
CONFIRMED 2026-08-31 (supersedes the original "synthesis never fires" framing).

Synthesis DOES fire and succeed. A push at 16:28:03 that carried two genuinely new observations produced synthesis-status.json {"outcome":"ok","timestamp":"2026-08-31T16:29:07.624Z"} on the Fly volume, and rewrote PERSONA.md from 118 to 134 lines. The ISS-045/046/047 fixes are all working in production.

The original symptom is explained by the ticket's own leading hypothesis, now confirmed: the 15:56:26 push carried zero new rows (the client's pushSince cursor had already advanced past them on an earlier push), so `obsAdded > 0` was false and nothing was enqueued. No status file was written because synthesize() was correctly never called.

THE REAL DEFECT is the second-order consequence, which is worse than the reported one. handleSyncPush both GATES ON and FEEDS FROM the current push's delta (`payload.observations`), not from unsynthesized input:

  const meaningful = payload.observations.filter((o) => o.confidence !== "low");
  if (obsAdded > 0 && meaningful.length > 0) { ... observations: meaningful ... }

Because src/sync.ts push() advances `pushSince` past everything it sent, an observation is offered to synthesis EXACTLY ONCE. If that one synthesis attempt fails — which it did on every attempt for three months under the ISS-045 timeout — those observations are never retried and never reach PERSONA. The client cursor has moved on and no later push re-sends them.

MEASURED LOSS: 66 observations dated 2026-05-28 through 2026-08-31 were delivered to the server (they are in observations.jsonl) but are absent from PERSONA. The 16:29 synthesis only saw the 2 observations that the last push happened to carry, which is why PERSONA jumped straight from "### 2026-05-24" to "[Current Session]" and skipped three months of accumulated signal.

FIX: gate on and feed from a per-tenant synthesis high-water mark rather than a single push's delta. Persist lastSynthesizedAt, select all meaningful observations newer than it, advance the mark ONLY after a successful synthesis writes PERSONA. A failed synthesis then retries the same batch on the next push instead of dropping it.
resolution:
Fixed in f3ce6a6, deployed and verified in production 2026-08-31.

ROOT CAUSE: handleSyncPush both gated on and fed from `payload.observations` — the current push's delta. Because src/sync.ts advances the client's `pushSince` past everything it sends, an observation was offered to synthesis exactly once; if that attempt failed (as every attempt did for three months under the ISS-045 timeout), it was never retried and never reached PERSONA. The reported symptom (a push synthesizing nothing) was the same defect from the other side: a duplicate push had obsAdded === 0.

FIX: a server-owned `lastSynthesizedAt` cursor in the existing per-tenant synthesis-status.json. Each push selects every meaningful observation newer than the cursor, oldest first; the cursor advances only after synthesize() returns non-null AND persona/playbook/active are written, so a failed attempt retries the same batch. recordSynthesisOutcome carries the cursor forward so an outcome write cannot reset it. Advance is monotonic and compares instants rather than strings (observation timestamps are inconsistently stamped with and without milliseconds; those forms do not sort lexicographically). Batches capped at 200 to bound the prompt; the remainder drains on later pushes because the cursor only moves to the end of what was fed.

SCOPE: server.ts's session-end path has no equivalent defect — its `mode !== "synced"` branch appends observations to PERSONA verbatim BEFORE enqueuing synthesis, so failure degrades rather than drops. `synced` mode neither appends nor synthesizes locally, which is why the loss was total and silent for synced clients only.

PRODUCTION VERIFICATION (the recovery this fix was meant to perform):
- Deployed; getSynthesisHighWater / advanceSynthesisHighWater confirmed present in /app/dist.
- Recovery push at 16:42 fed the whole pending backlog. At 16:44:04 the server wrote {"outcome":"ok","timestamp":"2026-08-31T16:44:04.983Z","lastSynthesizedAt":"2026-08-31T16:35:30.593Z"} — the cursor exists and is set to the newest observation.
- PERSONA.md grew 134 -> 207 lines. Topics from the previously-lost 2026-05-28..2026-08-31 window are now present and were absent before: Augur (4 hits), Monarch (2), commercialization (2), pricing (1), karuna mobile (1), parallel execution (4). The model absorbed them into the thematic sections rather than appending dated blocks, which is what the synthesis prompt asks for.
- Idempotence confirmed: a second push with nothing pending did NOT re-synthesize — status timestamp stayed at 16:44:04. The cursor correctly suppresses redundant work.

TESTS: src/sync-server-synthesis-gate.test.ts (7 cases; 3 failed against the old gate) plus 6 cursor-semantics cases in storage.test.ts. Suite 279 passed, tsc --noEmit clean.

Pre-recovery snapshot of PERSONA/PLAYBOOK/ACTIVE in docs/snapshots/2026-08-31-server-*.md (349ba65), since writePersonaAtomic keeps no backup.

FOLLOW-UP: ISS-049 remains open and is what made this invisible — synthesis-status.json is not in the sync pull payload, so no synced client (or the dashboard's LAST SYNTHESIS tile) can see outcome or the new lastSynthesizedAt cursor.
title: Synthesis gated on push delta, not unsynthesized input — silently drops observations from PERSONA
